'''''Sonchus ustulatus''''', also known as a '''leituga''',<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Macronesian |url=http://www.macaronesian.org/en/show/leituga-sonchus-ustulatus |website=Macronesian}}</ref> is a species of [[herb]] in the [[Asteraceae]] family. It is endemic to [[Madeira]], an island group in the Atlantic which is politically part of Portugal. It grows to be around 0.2 meters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sonchus ustulatus Lowe - Encyclopedia of Life |url=https://eol.org/pages/6251173 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=eol.org}}</ref>

== Description ==
The leituga is a [[perennial plant]] that either has no stem or a very short one. It does not have many floral heads and generally grows on a rocky [[Shore|shoreline]]. It is [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]].<ref name=":0" />

== Subspecies ==
The leituga has 2 [[subspecies]]:

* ''Sonchus ustulatus subsp. ustulatus'' 
* ''Sonchus ustulatus subsp. mederensis'' (Syn.: ''S. latifolius'') <ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=''Sonchus ustulatus'' Lowe - Encyclopedia of Life |url=https://eol.org/pages/6251173 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=eol.org}}</ref>
[[File:Sonchus ustulatus subsp. ustulatus.jpg|right|thumb|''Sonchus ustulatus'' subsp. ''ustulatus'', in [[Câmara de Lobos]], Madeira]]
